title: The Slot That Ran Inside Itself: processEvents in a Handler, Nested Calls and a Variable That Changed Under Its Owner

questions.question: A handler calls QCoreApplication::processEvents() in the middle of its work, and a second reading arrives for the same handler while it is working. What happens?
options: The second is delivered to the same handler from inside the call to processEvents, before the first has finished
questions.explanation: The log was begin 1, begin 2, end 2, begin 3, end 3, end 1.

questions.question: With readings 2 and 3 arriving while 1 is in progress, how deep was the nesting?
options: 2: Qt does not deliver an event again from a nested call while its own batch is being delivered
questions.explanation: 3 waited for 2. Reading 1 came back to find the member holding 3.

questions.question: Why does the corruption show under load and not on the bench?
options: It depends on whether a reading arrives while another is in progress, and on the bench they arrive slowly
The bench has a faster loop
questions.explanation: Which reading is hit depends on the timing.

questions.question: What does a busy flag that refuses a second call do wrong?
questions.explanation: What is wanted is that the call waits its turn in a line. The guard in the lesson queues instead of refusing.

questions.question: With the guard, what did the log look like, and how deep was the nesting?
options: begin 1, begin 2, begin 3, end 3, end 2, end 1 at depth 3
begin 1, end 1, begin 2, end 2, begin 3, end 3 at depth 1
questions.explanation: 200 queued readings were each handled once, in order.

questions.question: What is the better fix for a handler that is too slow?
options: Do the work somewhere else, on another thread (lesson 09-03)
questions.explanation: The handler returns to the loop on its own. The guard makes the handler safe and does not make processEvents a good idea.
